$comment: Regression gate thresholds — Phase 7 of docs/EVAL_HARNESS.md.
quality: absolute drop tolerated, as a positive number. 0.03 = fail if it falls >3 points.
A quality metric fails only when the drop clears the threshold AND the paired
95% CI excludes zero, so a drop inside the noise band cannot fail a build.
The spec names the latency key p95TotalMs; the harness writes totalMs.p95. The real
key is used, because gating on a metric that does not exist guards nothing quietly.
resource: relative rise tolerated. 0.25 = fail if it grows >25%. No CI: a p95 is an
aggregate, not a per-question value, and cannot be paired. These compare the
runs AS EXECUTED, so a cold run against a cached one differs enormously while
doing identical work — the gate warns when cache hit rates diverge.
correctness IS ADDED to the spec's default list, because it is the only judge Phase 3
actually validated (kappa 0.86, n=55) and it is the one with real variance: 52.4% on
the dev split, tracking recall almost exactly. A gate whose judge metrics are all
pinned at 1.0 guards nothing; this is the one that can move when generation breaks.
ON faithfulness, DELIBERATELY LEFT IN AT 0.05: it scored 1.0 on all 39 non-refusal
answers of the full dev split, so it currently has no variance and this threshold can
only catch a collapse, not a drift. Kept because a collapse is worth catching and the
cost of carrying it is zero. Do not read a green faithfulness gate as evidence.
refusalAccuracy sits at 1.0 on all 13 unanswerable questions for the same reason.
